facts.text: The DVD box of The Asylum's Halloween Night claims it's "Based On The Terrifying True Story That Started It All." Asylum boss David Michael Latt's explanation: a prank at his own Halloween party.
Latt says the "true story" was a party at a secluded house where guests were told a mental patient had escaped. When the prank kicked in, they believed the escapee had crashed the party.
Early script: Chris Vale was to be burned alive when a sofa he hid under caught fire. Fire-safety worries at the Asylum office building where they filmed led to the steam-pipe burn instead.
The DVD back cover carried a quote praising it as "A horror masterpiece from FANGORIA's Michael Gingold." Dread Central's review mocked it as a phantom quote.
Halloween Night is credited to Michael Gingold, a longtime Fangoria horror journalist who became the magazine's editor-in-chief in 2015. He also wrote the horror films Leeches and Ring of Darkness.
Halloween Night's cover art and plot were inspired by John Carpenter's 1978 Halloween, per IMDb trivia. The Asylum has built a business on cheap films that echo bigger ones.
The Asylum says it has never lost money on a film. Its low-budget movies reportedly earn around $150,000 to $250,000 in profit each.
In 2005 The Asylum released H. G. Wells' War of the Worlds a day before Spielberg's. Blockbuster ordered 100,000 copies, which pushed the studio toward mockbusters like this one.
Goof alert: as Todd picks up his knife from the floor and stands, a cameraman can be spotted in the mirror on the left side of the frame.
The film's opening disclaimer jokes: "We suggest moving and/or making sure no one was killed in your home BEFORE moving in."
Rebekah Kochan, who plays Shannon, is best known as Tiffani von der Sloot in the gay comedy franchise Eating Out.
Rebekah Kochan (Shannon) started acting at age nine, as the lead in a Las Vegas stage production of Annie. In 2006 she also made When a Killer Calls and Bram Stoker's Dracula's Curse.
Scot Nery (Chris Vale) later appeared in Bratz (2007), You Don't Mess with the Zohan (2008) and Scary Movie 5 (2013).
Scot Nery (Chris Vale) has been a pro entertainer since age 11, starting with magic shows in Ohio. In 2015 he launched Scot Nery's Boobie Trap, a weekly Hollywood variety show.
The end credits include a mock disclaimer: "No beautiful co-eds were hurt during the production of this screenplay. Only a really ugly dude so who cares?"
The end credits tell viewers to "Go back to the video store now and rent another Asylum film. You know you want to."
The soundtrack mixes bands like Strange Radio ("I Like Money") and Body Soil ("Battle of the Sexists") with a Jazz Farm track titled "Chicken & Bitches."
Goof alert: around the 30-minute mark a boom microphone can be seen on the back of the character Kendall.
Continuity goof: Chris Vale's face is blackened and burned, but once he puts on a victim's costume mask, his face through the eyeholes looks perfectly fine.
Dread Central rated it 2 out of 5. It said the only original kill involves a coat hanger and the rest are routine axe hacks and throat slashings.
Per IMDb, Halloween Night has in-jokes and nods to Frankenstein (1931), the grim indie Gummo (1997) and Girls Gone Wild on Campus 2 (2003).
Director Mark Atkins' first feature, Night Orchid, won Best First Feature Film at the New Orleans Film Festival. He became one of The Asylum's most in-demand directors and cinematographers.
Goof alert: as Todd and Christopher head down the stairs, lighting equipment is visible on the right side of the frame.
Jim McLennan of Film Blitz gave it a C+, calling it "a cheerfully shallow slasher, with little or no pretension" and praising its make-up and effects work.
Filming took place around Lake Arrowhead in the San Bernardino National Forest and in Norwalk, California.

Film Threat's Steve Anderson called it "truly abysmal" and said it makes him "weep for the genre," yet admitted: "I'm still glad I watched it." He said it mashes Halloween with Friday the 13th Part 2.
Wikipedia notes the film spoofs Halloween H20 (1998). It was in turn spoofed in Boogeyman 2 (2007).
The film's killer wears a costume that includes a Quiet Riot mask, a hand axe, a sword and a big wavy knife, all taken from a victim.
Dread Central compared the look of the burned Chris Vale to the Land of the Dead zombies and Darkman, calling it a rubbery mix of both.
Popcorn Pictures argued killer Chris Vale doesn't work as a slasher: he's "very much human" and gets beaten up, unlike unstoppable monsters Michael Myers and Jason Voorhees.
Reviewer Andrew Smith at Popcorn Pictures called it "a terrible Halloween rip-off" and said it would work better with a lighter, self-aware tone.
Cinema Crazed gave it 1 out of 4 stars. Felix Vasquez Jr. wrote that "as a Halloween wannabe, it's horrible, but as a slasher film on its own merits it's horrible."
Alicia Klein, who plays Tracy, made her screen debut in Halloween Night, per IMDb trivia.
The Asylum's film credits include Mega Shark vs. Giant Octopus and, in 2013, Sharknado, the studio's biggest hit.
The film got a later shout-out: The Asylum: Case Studies (2021) references Halloween Night, per IMDb's connections list.
Goof: David Baxter (Derek Osedach) lies dead with his mouth half open. After a cutaway to Shannon (Rebekah Kochan), the body's mouth is closed.
